title: BSI Authentication login and recovery pilot
limitations: Planning-only pilot: no test case was executed and every status is not_run.
No target URL, authorized account, OTP sandbox, or runtime contract was provided.
AuthenticationService is supplied by external package @bsi/auth-core 4.1.3 and was not source-reviewed.
The referenced login APIs are not implemented in the supplied bsi-auth-api-example repository.
Both application worktrees contain unrelated local changes; analyzed login files were not modified.

test_cases.scenario: Login alias redirects to the canonical login route
steps: Observe the final route and component
test_cases.expected_result: The router resolves to /account/login and renders LoginComponent without a redirect loop.

test_cases.scenario: Empty username and password cannot be submitted
test_cases.expected_result: Submit remains disabled and required-field feedback is visible for both fields.

test_cases.scenario: Only username populated remains invalid
test_cases.expected_result: The form stays invalid and no authentication request is sent.

test_cases.scenario: Valid credentials navigate to the approved redirect URL
test_cases.expected_result: One login request succeeds and the user reaches the approved redirect route.

test_cases.scenario: Unknown username and wrong password produce equivalent safe failures
preconditions: Authorized test endpoint and rate ceiling
steps: Submit a known test username with wrong password
Compare status, body, visible message, and timing
test_cases.expected_result: Failures do not disclose whether an account exists and do not expose internal details.
test_cases.notes: Active security comparison needs explicit authorization.

test_cases.scenario: Repeated submit while loading initiates one request
test_cases.expected_result: The button remains disabled while loading and only one service call is initiated.

test_cases.scenario: Production hides direct login controls by default
test_cases.expected_result: Direct-login controls are hidden while approved SSO entry points remain available.

test_cases.scenario: Developer query override follows approved production policy
preconditions: Explicit authorization to evaluate alternate production auth surface
steps: Open production login with a truthy developer query
test_cases.expected_result: Behavior matches an explicitly approved policy and cannot bypass server-side authentication controls.
test_cases.notes: Do not execute against production without technique-level authorization.

test_cases.scenario: Member and parent SSO links use environment configuration
test_cases.expected_result: Both links are present and match the approved destinations for the environment.

test_cases.scenario: Valid SSO callback authenticates and redirects
preconditions: Authorized SSO sandbox and callback identity
test_cases.expected_result: The callback is accepted once and the user reaches the approved redirect route.

test_cases.scenario: Invalid or expired SSO callback is rejected safely
steps: Open callback with an invalid sandbox token
test_cases.expected_result: Authentication is rejected, no session is established, and a safe error is displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Opening login without a query token invokes logout once
test_cases.expected_result: Logout is called once and no SSO login call is made.
test_cases.notes: Product owner must confirm the desired session UX.

test_cases.scenario: Authentication secrets do not leak through browser surfaces
steps: Inspect address history, referrer behavior, console, analytics, and logs
test_cases.expected_result: No reusable secret is retained or disclosed beyond the approved exchange boundary.

test_cases.scenario: Malformed SSO callback path fails without unsafe navigation
preconditions: LoginSSOComponent is isolated with a mocked auth service
steps: Provide missing or extra path segments
test_cases.expected_result: Malformed paths are rejected predictably without logging secrets or navigating to an unintended route.

test_cases.scenario: 2FA-enabled primary login shows the authenticator form
preconditions: Mock primary login succeeds with enable2Fa true
test_cases.expected_result: Direct navigation does not occur and the required authenticator form is displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Empty authenticator code cannot be submitted
test_cases.expected_result: The form remains invalid and verify2FA is not called.

test_cases.scenario: Valid authenticator code completes login
test_cases.expected_result: Verification succeeds once and navigation reaches the approved redirect route.

test_cases.scenario: Wrong, expired, reused, and cross-account codes are rejected
preconditions: Authorized 2FA API contract and test identities
steps: Submit each invalid code class within the approved rate
test_cases.expected_result: Every invalid class is rejected and no full session is issued.

test_cases.scenario: Post-login resources cannot be accessed before second-factor verification
test_cases.expected_result: Pre-MFA state cannot access resources requiring full authentication.

test_cases.scenario: Repeated invalid codes are throttled according to contract
preconditions: Approved attempt ceiling and disposable 2FA account
steps: Submit invalid codes up to the approved boundary
test_cases.expected_result: Attempts are bounded without uncontrolled account denial-of-service and recovery follows policy.
test_cases.notes: Rate and lockout policy must be supplied before execution.

test_cases.scenario: Forgot-password action switches from login to recovery
steps: Inspect visible forms and initial state
test_cases.expected_result: Login/2FA forms are replaced by the account-recovery entry state with no retained credential values.

test_cases.scenario: Account verification request matches the approved API contract
test_cases.expected_result: The request, status, response envelope, and error behavior conform to the approved contract.

test_cases.scenario: Known and unknown accounts receive enumeration-safe recovery responses
steps: Request recovery for known test account
Request recovery for unknown synthetic account
Compare status, body, timing, and UI
test_cases.expected_result: Responses do not disclose account existence beyond approved policy.

test_cases.scenario: Verified test account receives one sandbox OTP request
preconditions: Authorized test account and WhatsApp sandbox
test_cases.expected_result: One request is recorded, loading settles, and the OTP entry state is enabled without exposing the code.

test_cases.scenario: Valid OTP advances once and returns a scoped reset token
preconditions: Authorized recovery account and current sandbox OTP
steps: Attempt safe reuse according to contract
test_cases.expected_result: The flow advances once, a scoped token is returned securely, and reuse is rejected.

test_cases.scenario: Wrong, expired, reused, and cross-account recovery codes are rejected
preconditions: Authorized recovery test identities and rate ceiling
test_cases.expected_result: Every invalid class is rejected without issuing a reset token or leaking account data.

test_cases.scenario: Mismatched password confirmation is prevented or rejected clearly
test_cases.expected_result: The mismatch is blocked with specific feedback and no password change occurs.
test_cases.notes: Current client-side match validation was not found.

test_cases.scenario: Password policy boundaries are enforced consistently by UI and API
preconditions: Approved password and reset API contract
steps: Submit authorized synthetic values at policy boundaries
test_cases.expected_result: UI and API consistently enforce the approved policy without exposing password values.

test_cases.scenario: Reset token is account-bound, short-lived, single-use, and invalid after success
steps: Use a valid sandbox reset token once
test_cases.expected_result: Only the valid first use succeeds; all other classes are rejected without account change.

test_cases.scenario: Successful reset follows the approved session and token invalidation policy
preconditions: Disposable account with approved pre-reset sessions
test_cases.expected_result: Old sessions/tokens are invalidated according to the approved recovery policy.

test_cases.scenario: Back action clears local recovery secrets and flags
preconditions: Recovery flow contains account, OTP, token, and password state
test_cases.expected_result: Recovery identifiers, OTP, token, passwords, errors, loading, and visibility return to the initial login state.

test_cases.scenario: All login, SSO, 2FA, recovery, and back actions are keyboard operable
preconditions: Supported desktop browser and no mouse input
steps: Traverse the entire flow by keyboard
test_cases.expected_result: Interactive elements are reachable in logical order, visibly focused, and operable without a pointer.

test_cases.scenario: Inputs have programmatic names and errors are associated with fields
test_cases.expected_result: Every control has an unambiguous programmatic name and each error is perceivable and associated with its field.
test_cases.notes: Placeholders alone may not satisfy the approved accessibility target.

test_cases.scenario: Loading, errors, success, and step transitions are announced
steps: Trigger loading, validation, service failure, OTP success, and reset success states
test_cases.expected_result: Dynamic states are perceivable without relying only on color or visual position, and focus moves predictably.
